claims.text: The proposed framework independently computes lattice and electronic heat transport rather than treating them as a single contribution.
The proposed framework will predict the total thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than earlier combined-parameter models.
The discrepancy from experiment will be reduced by at least 50% relative to earlier models.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are nearly equal.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr remains nearly constant from 300 to 1200 K.
The electronic thermal-conductivity contribution of HfNbTaTiZr increases with temperature at high temperature.
The target initial state is a defect-free, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Experimental HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen are available.
The total thermal conductivity measured between 300 and 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K m).
Machine-learned force fields with on-the-fly anharmonic corrections and Green–Kubo analysis will be used for lattice transport.
First-principles Boltzmann transport calculations will be used for electronic heat transport.
Intrinsic local lattice distortions occur in HfNbTaTiZr because of chemical and atomic-size disorder.
Oxygen induces additional local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local lattice distortions separately modulate phonon scattering and electron mobility.
Explicit treatment of anharmonic lattice dynamics will improve prediction of the lattice contribution.
Explicit treatment of electron scattering from chemical disorder will improve prediction of the electronic contribution.
Separating the heat carriers minimizes errors caused by simplified Debye-temperature estimates and mean-field approximations.
Earlier approaches often used simplified Debye models and did not distinguish lattice from electronic heat transfer.
The model's improved accuracy is limited to chemically homogeneous, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr specimens whose oxygen and defect contents are accurately characterized.
TDTR can provide the lattice contribution while terahertz spectroscopy or electrical-resistivity measurements can provide the electronic contribution for a decisive channel-separated comparison.

contradictions.description: The 10–17 W/(K m) range is described in the conditions as a measured high-temperature total conductivity, but the baseline recasts the same range as a spread of earlier model predictions.
